fans notes.title: A Fan's Notes
fans notes.author: Frederick Exley
fans notes.why: A man obsessed with football and the New York Giants unravels; readers call it hilarious and sad.

eight.title: The Eight
eight.author: Katherine Neville
eight.why: Two women centuries apart chase a chess set with secret powers; a real page-turner.

light fantastic.title: The Light Fantastic
light fantastic.author: Terry Pratchett
light fantastic.why: The second Discworld book continues the wizard Rincewind's misadventures; adored even though it is rarely praised.

footfall.title: Footfall
footfall.author: Larry Niven and Jerry Pournelle
footfall.why: Elephant-like aliens invade Earth in an engaging hard-SF clash; great alien-invasion fun.

none of this is true.title: None of This Is True
none of this is true.author: Lisa Jewell
none of this is true.why: Two women with shared birthdays and a podcast, with a plot twist readers loved.

factotum.title: Factotum
factotum.author: Charles Bukowski
factotum.why: Bukowski's alter ego drifts through dead-end jobs and bars; raw, coarse and short.

alice.title: Alice
alice.author: Christina Henry
alice.why: A very dark retelling of Alice in Wonderland with trafficking and violence; flagged for content warnings.

chronicles of thomas covenant.title: The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant
chronicles of thomas covenant.author: Stephen R. Donaldson
chronicles of thomas covenant.why: A leper is thrown into a fantasy world he refuses to believe in; an influential but heavy series.

jakarta method.title: The Jakarta Method
jakarta method.author: Vincent Bevins
jakarta method.why: How US-backed anti-communist killings in Indonesia shaped the Cold War; readers could not put it down.

clytemnestra.title: Clytemnestra
clytemnestra.author: Costanza Casati
clytemnestra.why: The Greek queen's story from princess to vengeful ruler; a favourite mythic retelling.

known world.title: The Known World
known world.author: Edward P. Jones
known world.why: A Black slaveowner in antebellum Virginia; a Pulitzer winner some call the best novel they have read.

commonwealth.title: Commonwealth
commonwealth.author: Ann Patchett
commonwealth.why: Two families are blended and reshaped over decades; a warm, perceptive novel.

tinkers.title: Tinkers
tinkers.author: Paul Harding
tinkers.why: A dying clockmaker's last days and his father's memories; poetic Pulitzer winner.

empire trilogy.title: The Empire Trilogy
empire trilogy.author: Raymond E. Feist
empire trilogy.why: Feist and Wurts's tale of political intrigue in a Tsurani-inspired empire; a standout in the Riftwar saga.

ilium.title: Ilium
ilium.author: Dan Simmons
ilium.why: The Trojan War is replayed by gods on Mars, with robots and scholars; a perfect sci-fi and fantasy blend.

garden spells.title: Garden Spells
garden spells.author: Sarah Addison Allen
garden spells.why: A woman with a magical garden and her sister in a small North Carolina town; sweet, easy and light.

inmate.title: The Inmate
inmate.author: Freida McFadden
inmate.why: A psychological thriller about a nurse at a prison; twisty page-turner fans.

demon cycle.title: Demon Cycle
demon cycle.author: Peter V. Brett
demon cycle.why: Mentioned mainly as a series that went off the rails.

firm.title: The Firm
firm.author: John Grisham
firm.why: A young lawyer discovers his firm's dark secrets; a classic legal thriller devoured on a single flight.

ghost.title: Ghost
ghost.author: Jason Reynolds
ghost.why: Comments are about different books named Ghost.

things.title: Things
things.author: Todd Thyberg
things.why: Comments refer to other works, not one clear book.

glamorama.title: Glamorama
glamorama.author: Bret Easton Ellis
glamorama.why: A model gets caught in a surreal terror plot in Ellis's satire of celebrity; wild and not for the faint of heart.

rats.title: Rats
rats.author: Robert Sullivan
rats.why: A year spent observing New York's rats; fascinating nature writing.

far from the madding crowd.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
far from the madding crowd.author: Thomas Hardy
far from the madding crowd.why: A spirited woman farmer attracts three suitors in rural England; turned one reader into a Hardy fan.

hooked.title: Hooked
hooked.author: Asako Yuzuki
hooked.why: A woman befriends a blogger she admires and things turn unsettling; a good Japanese novel, though not as good as Butter.

story of edgar sawtelle.title: The story of Edgar Sawtelle
story of edgar sawtelle.author: David Wroblewski
story of edgar sawtelle.why: A mute boy and his family's dogs, retold from Hamlet; readers say it made them bawl.

all my puny sorrows.title: All My Puny Sorrows
all my puny sorrows.author: Miriam Toews
all my puny sorrows.why: Two sisters, one suicidal; heartbreaking yet funny.

white tiger.title: The White Tiger
white tiger.author: Aravind Adiga
white tiger.why: A servant narrates his rise from poverty in India through crime; a savage, funny class satire.

inversions.title: Inversions
inversions.author: Iain Banks
inversions.why: A Culture novel set in a medieval-style world; beautiful for some, a slog for others.

northern lights.title: Northern Lights
northern lights.author: Philip Pullman
northern lights.why: A girl travels north with an alethiometer and a daemon; the novel that turned a non-reader into a reader.

four agreements.title: The Four Agreements
four agreements.author: Don Miguel Ruiz
four agreements.why: Four simple rules for personal freedom; short, clear and helpful for many readers.

demon of unrest.title: The Demon of Unrest
demon of unrest.author: Erik Larson
demon of unrest.why: The months between Lincoln's election and the Fort Sumter attack; compelling but long and slow for some.

grant.title: Grant
grant.author: Ron Chernow
grant.why: A big biography of Ulysses S. Grant; absorbing despite the 1000-plus pages.

christy.title: Christy
christy.author: Catherine Marshall
christy.why: A young teacher goes to an Appalachian mission school in 1912; a beloved, inspiring read.

foe.title: Foe
foe.author: Iain Reid
foe.why: A farm couple faces a stranger offering to replace the husband; short, eerie and engaging.

iron flame.title: Iron Flame
iron flame.author: Rebecca Yarros
iron flame.why: Mostly criticised for its romance-heavy plot.

babel 17.title: Babel-17
babel 17.author: Samuel R. Delany
babel 17.why: A poet-linguist decodes an enemy language that shapes thought; a gem of classic sci-fi.

skeleton crew.title: Skeleton crew
skeleton crew.author: Stephen King
skeleton crew.why: King's collection of short stories and novellas, including The Jaunt; varied and scary.

traitor.title: Traitor
traitor.author: Matthew Woodring Stover
traitor.why: A New Jedi Order novel regarded as the series' peak and one of the best Star Wars books.

red winter.title: The Red Winter
red winter.author: Cameron Sullivan
red winter.why: A fantasy-horror novel readers began and enjoyed; a new release with early positive buzz.

britt marie was here.title: Britt-Marie Was Here
britt marie was here.author: Fredrik Backman
britt marie was here.why: A cranky woman reinvents herself in a small town; warm and funny Backman.

paradais.title: Paradais
paradais.author: Fernanda Melchor
paradais.why: Two teens in a gated Mexican community plan something terrible; short, wild and disturbing.

star trek.title: Star Trek
star trek.author: Gene Roddenberry
star trek.why: Comments are about the TV franchise, not a book.

barneys version.title: Barney's Version
barneys version.author: Mordecai Richler
barneys version.why: A cranky Montrealer's memoirs with a murder mystery; funny without trying to be.

black boy.title: Black Boy
black boy.author: Richard Wright
black boy.why: Richard Wright's story of growing up Black in the Jim Crow South; a memoir that readers recall for its power.

keeper of the lost cities.title: Keeper of the Lost Cities
keeper of the lost cities.author: Shannon Messenger
keeper of the lost cities.why: A girl finds she is an elf with telepathic powers; a series fans love and read together.

in other lands.title: In Other Lands
in other lands.author: Sarah Rees Brennan
in other lands.why: A boy enters a school at the edge of a magical world; underrated and an all-time favourite for its fans.

harpo speaks.title: Harpo Speaks!
harpo speaks.author: Harpo Marx
harpo speaks.why: Harpo Marx's life from vaudeville to Hollywood; a warm tale of a genius and a mensch.

dovekeepers.title: The Dovekeepers
dovekeepers.author: Alice Hoffman
dovekeepers.why: Four women endure the siege of Masada; hauntingly beautiful.

year of the flood.title: The Year of the Flood
year of the flood.author: Margaret Atwood
year of the flood.why: The second MaddAddam book follows survivors of a plague and a religious sect; some like it better than the first.

lady susan.title: Lady Susan
lady susan.author: Jane Austen
lady susan.why: Austen's epistolary novella about a manipulative widow; wicked and unlike her other books, though one reader disliked it.

lolita by vladimir nabokov.title: Lolita
lolita by vladimir nabokov.author: Vladimir Nabokov
lolita by vladimir nabokov.why: A scholarly predator narrates his obsession; a beautifully written but disturbing classic.

theft of fire.title: Theft of Fire
theft of fire.author: Devon Eriksen
theft of fire.why: A hard-SF adventure in the asteroid belt with a competent hero; devoted fans call it an addictive read.

not my fathers son.title: Not My Father's Son
not my fathers son.author: Alan Cumming
not my fathers son.why: An actor uncovers his abusive father's past and family secrets; stays with readers years later.

miss peregrines home for peculiar childr.title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
miss peregrines home for peculiar childr.author: Ransom Riggs
miss peregrines home for peculiar childr.why: A boy discovers a hidden home for peculiar kids, told with vintage photographs; more horror than fantasy.

shoe dog.title: Shoe Dog
shoe dog.author: Phil Knight
shoe dog.why: Phil Knight tells how he built Nike; so readable that non-readers finished it in a week.

damned.title: Damned
damned.author: Chuck Palahniuk
damned.why: Mentioned mostly for its disliked narrator.

this immortal.title: This Immortal
this immortal.author: Roger Zelazny
this immortal.why: An immortal official guides an alien tourist through a ruined Earth; a Zelazny classic with a mythic feel.

female man.title: The Female Man
female man.author: Joanna Russ
female man.why: Four women from different worlds confront sexism; a challenging classic of feminist sci-fi.

happy place.title: Happy Place
happy place.author: Emily Henry
happy place.why: Mostly criticised by readers who did not enjoy the hype.

fever house.title: Fever House
fever house.author: Keith Rosson
fever house.why: A strange, disorienting horror about a secret lab and an unleashed disaster; absolute madness, according to fans.

library book.title: The Library Book
library book.author: Susan Orlean
library book.why: Susan Orlean investigates the 1986 Los Angeles Library fire and celebrates libraries; fascinating and well written.

time shelter.title: Time Shelter
time shelter.author: Georgi Gospodinov
time shelter.why: A man opens clinics that recreate the past for dementia patients; a brilliant, sad allegory about memory.

lone women.title: Lone Women
lone women.author: Victor D. LaValle
lone women.why: A woman homesteads in 1915 Montana with a terrible secret in her trunk; a feminist western horror.

wetlands.title: Wetlands
wetlands.author: Charlotte Roche
wetlands.why: A young woman in hospital recounts her bodily obsessions with unflinching candour; you need a strong stomach.

silent spring.title: Silent Spring
silent spring.author: Rachel Carson
silent spring.why: Rachel Carson's exposé of pesticides that sparked the environmental movement; a book that made readers lifelong advocates.

stone diaries.title: The Stone Diaries
stone diaries.author: Carol Shields
stone diaries.why: An ordinary woman's life told through shifting narrators; quiet and subtle, not to everyone's taste.

many lives of mama love.title: The Many Lives of Mama Love
many lives of mama love.author: Lara Love Hardin
many lives of mama love.why: A mother's journey from addiction and prison to writing; a moving, redemptive memoir.

heart of a dog.title: Heart of a Dog
heart of a dog.author: Mikhail Bulgakov
heart of a dog.why: A scientist turns a stray dog into a man in this Soviet satire; a slept-on masterpiece.
